\tabnotes{The dependent variable is the local-currency $\rxbar_{i,t+12}$. The
  $\CF$ and $\GCF$ columns under $R^{2}$ report the single-factor fits of the
  local regression \eqref{eq:h-local} and the global regression
  \eqref{eq:h-global}; the Joint column reports the horse race
  $\rxbar_{i,t+12}=\alpha_i+\beta_i\,\CF^{\perp}_{i,t}+\gamma_i\,\GCF_{t}
  +\varepsilon_{i,t+12}$ \eqref{eq:h-horse}, where $\CF^{\perp}_{i,t}$ is the
  part of the local factor orthogonal to $\GCF_{t}$, following
  \citet{dahlquist2013}. The HAC $t$ columns report Newey--West $t$-statistics
  on the two slopes of the joint regression. Wald $p$ is the $p$-value of the
  joint test of no predictability, and $p$ (BH) applies the
  Benjamini--Hochberg false-discovery-rate adjustment across the eleven
  markets. A significant $\GCF$ together with an insignificant $\CF^{\perp}$
  signals that the global factor subsumes the local factor. The final row adds
  country fixed effects on the pooled G10 panel (Benjamini--Hochberg not
  applicable).}
